# Implement block: Sketch Coffee Splash (React Native)

You are adding the "Sketch Coffee Splash" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

A launch screen for an invented coffee shop, Inkpot Coffee Co., drawn entirely as white hand-inked line art on ultramarine. The welcome reads "Welcome to our coffee haven!" with "haven!" in a handwritten marker, a small address and handwritten opening hours, a round arrow button, and a big tilted paper cup with coffee splashing out of it in a curling sheet and flying drops; every line is an uneven, tapered ink stroke that boils gently. In between, the screen clears to a top-view cup where a sketched hand and arm stir with a spoon while a handwritten percentage counts to 100, then the welcome and its splash bounce back in.

**Motion.** Every stroke is a ribbon built from a Catmull-Rom curve sampled every 2 pt: its centre line wobbles by up to about 1.3 pt (1.7 to 2 pt on the splash) along two sine waves of its length, its width swings between 80% and 108% of its nominal 3 to 6.6 pt and tapers at both ends over 16 pt, and a closed stroke runs 7% past its start like a pen overshooting its loop. Four wobble variants of every stroke are built once from a fixed seed and the art switches between them 8 times a second (the boil). The self-playing demo loops every 10 s (LOOP), starting and ending on the welcome at rest: 0 to 1.2 s rest, with the drops bobbing 2.4 pt on a 2.5 s sine; from 1.2 s the button shrinks to a dot over 0.22 s (ease-in) and fades over 0.13 s, the five title lines slide 110% of the width to the right over 0.5 s each (cubic ease-in, 0.04 s apart from 1.25 s) and the four notes 60% of the width to the left (from 1.3 s, 0.03 s apart), while the cup lifts 14 pt and drops away 80% of the width right and 34% of the height down, turning from -14 deg to +16 deg over 0.65 s (cubic ease-in). At 2.2 s a top-view cup (92 pt across, a pale blue shadow offset 6 pt down) pops up from nothing over 0.4 s (back-out, overshoot 2.0) and "0%" fades in from 2.35 s over 0.25 s; from 2.5 s the arm slides 460 pt up its own direction into place over 0.6 s (cubic ease-out). The spoon tip circles 17 pt from the cup's centre at 0.85 s a turn, its speed ramping in over 0.4 s from 2.95 s and out over 0.4 s from 6.55 s; the pinch follows 35% of the tip's movement, the arm turns to keep pointing at the same shoulder off screen, a swirl arc 24 pt out in the coffee runs ahead of the spoon (faded with its speed), and the percentage counts linearly from 3.0 s to 100% at 6.55 s. The hand pulls back out the way it came from 6.7 s over 0.45 s (cubic ease-in) and the cup shrinks away from 7.0 s over 0.3 s (back-in, so it swells a touch first) while the percentage fades over 0.25 s. From 7.3 s the button returns as a dot that grows into the 48 pt circle over 0.3 s (back-out 2.2), its chevron fading in over the last 40% of its growth; the title lines wipe back in from the right from 7.4 s and the notes from the left from 7.45 s (quintic ease-out over 0.75 s, 0.05 and 0.04 s apart); the paper cup bounces back from the bottom right on a damped spring (1 - e^-5u cos(2.5 pi u)(1 - u), about 8% overshoot) over 0.9 s from 7.5 s, untilting from +18 deg; the splash grows out of the rim on the same spring over 0.8 s from 7.75 s (55% to 100% wide, 0 to 100% tall); and the ten drops are thrown from the rim to their places over 0.6 s each from 7.8 s, 0.04 s apart (back-out 1.4), growing from 35%. All is at rest from 8.4 s to 10 s. Touch: a tap on the welcome plays the loader; while the spoon stirs, dragging clockwise round the cup (starting within 150 pt of it) takes over the spoon and pushes the percentage on, one turn of the finger moving the script on by one turn of the spoon, with a selection haptic every 10%, and on release the script carries on from there; a tap during the loader skips to 100% and the welcome; taps give a light haptic. The script's time is worked out from a start time, never accumulated, so the period stays constant. Under reduced motion the welcome is shown still, with no boil, no bobbing and no loop.

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
